note: Written by tools/build_page_text.py from book/ch15_token_cost.md, section 15.7; do not edit by hand.
what_worked: Every figure is calculated by Python from WDI and PWT data. The JavaScript version gives the same numbers for all 147 economy-years tested.
The template part gave an answer to all 24 questions in the Chapter 14 run and corrected q4-02's false premise.

The four kinds of mistake in the language model's output in Chapter 13 (wrong sign, false premise, added flags, escalation not called for; F15 to F18) cannot occur in the template part: each of those lines comes from a tested function.
In the run of 16 November, the checks dropped all 28 faulty explanations and showed none.
The vertical domain expert judged 19 of 20 cited sentences supported; the word-overlap check agreed on 17.
Routing: 56 of 56 bank questions (training); 19 of 32 new questions in the first fair test.
Definition questions: a correct passage in the top three for 31 of 32.
The licence filter in the vector database kept the same passages as the hand-written filter on all 32 questions.
Every score is labelled training or fair; fair tests were frozen in a commit before the questions were opened.
After the review, two explanations with content passed (f-07, f-08), training scores. In the rerun of 22 November, the vertical domain expert judged f-09 good.

Only the steps that call the language model use tokens: the explanation and, for definition questions, the answer extracted from passages. Lookups, series titles, clarifying and escalation are answered by code at no cost in tokens, and the steps in Python took under a tenth of a second for 24 questions.
what_a_production_version_needs: More accurate reading of typed questions in parts (economy, measure, year and edition). With keyword rules alone, the right figures were found for 2 of 20 new questions, and with a small language model for 9 of 20. In the page, each part is read separately, with rules and, for the measure, search by meaning, and the reading is shown for the user to correct: every part was right for 32 of 78 new questions, and the measure for 39 of 78. This can be improved by many more aliases for each measure in the controlled vocabulary, written by the vertical domain expert; and by a classifier trained on thousands of real users' questions, each labelled part by part. The demonstration version has only 134 questions written by us.
A larger language model, with sentence and id requested as separate fields.
Counts of both kinds of check error: good replies dropped and bad replies shown.

A check that a reply answers the question and that its conclusion follows from the passages. On 16 November f-09's retry did not answer the question; on 22 November the checks showed f-08, whose last sentence draws a conclusion about Ireland that no passage given supports.
A named horizontal domain expert who sets and reviews the size bands, consulting the vertical domain expert.
New questions from real users, scored before any rule changes.
More data and passages (a passage defining PPP; the production boundary for unpaid work at home).
Explanations and their cited passages in a form the vertical domain expert can review quickly.
The review list in a form the horizontal domain expert can read quickly.

A token and time limit for each route. On the laptop, an R2 question with an explanation took about 3,600 tokens in and 120 seconds; a retry added about 2,000 tokens and 29 seconds, and gave content only once out of 15 retries, an explanation judged a fault.

Cost per route times the number of questions asked gives the total, so a team can price a rise in use.
